question:
Which of the following statements about Mumbai's architectural heritage is/are correct?
1. Victorian Gothic buildings in Mumbai reflect colonial-era architecture with Neo-Gothic elements.
2. Art Deco buildings in Mumbai were part of the 19th-century colonial urban development.
3. The Oval Maidan distinctly separates the Victorian Gothic and Art Deco architectural styles.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1 and 3 are correct.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensembles of Mumbai (मुंबई के विक्टोरियन गोथिक और आर्ट डेको समूह) were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2018.

• Statement 1 is correct: Victorian Gothic buildings (e.g., the High Court, University of Mumbai) reflect colonial-era architecture with Neo-Gothic elements.

• Statement 3 is correct: The Oval Maidan is the open green space that clearly divides the 19th-century Victorian Gothic public buildings on one side from the 20th-century Art Deco buildings on the other.

• Statement 2 is incorrect: Art Deco architecture in Mumbai belongs to the 20th century (1930s), not the 19th century.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The ensemble lies around the Oval Maidan in South Mumbai's Fort precinct.

• Marine Drive's buildings form one of the largest Art Deco collections in the world.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Incorrect because it wrongly places Art Deco in the 19th century (Statement 2 is false).

• opt (Option 2): Incorrect because Statement 2 (Art Deco as 19th-century development) is false.

• opt (Option 4): Incorrect because Statement 2 is false, so not all three statements are correct.

question:
Fill in the blank:
The hornbill bird, after which the festival is named, symbolizes boldness and _____ in Naga folklore.
solution_text:
The correct answer is grandeur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Hornbill Festival (हॉर्नबिल महोत्सव) is celebrated every year from 1 to 10 December in Nagaland and is called the 'Festival of Festivals'.

• The festival is named after the Indian hornbill, a bird that features prominently in Naga folklore and tribal traditions.

• In Naga folklore, the hornbill symbolizes boldness and grandeur.

• The festival is held at the Naga Heritage Village, Kisama, near Kohima.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The festival was first launched in 2000 by the Government of Nagaland to encourage inter-tribal interaction and preserve cultural heritage.

• Nagaland is known as the 'Land of Festivals'.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): 'wisdom' is not the attribute associated with the hornbill in this context.

• opt (Option 2): 'prosperity' is not the symbolic meaning of the hornbill here.

• opt (Option 4): 'peace' is not associated with the hornbill in Naga folklore in this context.

question: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched in accordance with Gupta's administration (Officer-Stated Role)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Talavataka-Village Accountant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Gupta administration (गुप्त प्रशासन) had a well-organised bureaucracy with officials at central, provincial and village levels.

• At the village level, the Talavataka functioned as the village accountant/record keeper.

• The correctly matched pair here is Talavataka – Village Accountant.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Gupta empire was divided into provinces (Bhuktis) headed by Uparikas and districts (Vishayas) headed by Vishayapatis.

• Village administration was carried out by the Gramika and local village bodies.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Dhruvadhikaranika was linked to land-revenue records/collection, not the treasury, so 'Treasurer' is wrongly matched.

• opt (Option 2): Bhandagaradhikrita headed the treasury/storehouse (Bhandagara), not the police, so 'Chief of Police' is wrongly matched.

• opt (Option 4): Utkhetayita is not correctly matched with 'Land-Survey Officer' in this pairing (marked wrong).

question: Which classical musical treatise, composed in the 13th century CE by Sharangadeva in Maharashtra, is considered a foundational text in Indian musicology?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sangeet Ratnakara.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sangeet Ratnakara (संगीत रत्नाकर) was composed by Sharangadeva (Sarngadeva) in the 13th century CE in the Deccan (Maharashtra) region.

• It is regarded as a foundational text of Indian musicology, dealing with both Hindustani and Carnatic music traditions.

• The text was written during the reign of the Yadava dynasty at Devagiri.

• It is often called the 'Ocean of Music and Dance' and covers svara, raga, tala and dance.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Because it precedes the sharp Hindustani-Carnatic split, both systems refer to it as authoritative.

• It systematically describes 264 ragas.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Natya Shastra was composed by Bharata Muni and deals with dramaturgy, not the 13th-century treatise in question.

• opt (Option 2): Sangeet Sudha is a later musicological work, not the 13th-century foundational text.

• opt (Option 4): Abhinaya Darpana by Nandikeshvara is a treatise on dance gestures (abhinaya), not this musical treatise.

question: When was the Amateur Athletics Federation of India (AAFI) established?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1946.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Amateur Athletics Federation of India (भारतीय एमेच्योर एथलेटिक्स महासंघ) was established in 1946.

• It is the apex body governing athletics (track and field) in India.

• It is now known as the Athletics Federation of India (AFI).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The AFI is affiliated to World Athletics (formerly IAAF) and the Asian Athletics Association.

• The current headquarters of the AFI is in New Delhi.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): 1936 is incorrect; it is the year of the Berlin Olympics, not the AAFI's establishment.

• opt (Option 3): 1956 is incorrect and does not mark the AAFI's foundation.

• opt (Option 4): 1966 is incorrect and does not mark the AAFI's foundation.

question:
Fill in the blank:
After defeating the Mughal emperor, _______ declared himself the ruler and founded the Second Afghan Empire.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sher Shah Suri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sher Shah Suri (शेर शाह सूरी) defeated the Mughal emperor Humayun at the Battle of Chausa (1539) and the Battle of Kannauj/Bilgram (1540).

• After defeating Humayun, he declared himself ruler and founded the Sur Empire, often called the Second Afghan Empire.

• His original name was Farid Khan; he earned the title 'Sher Khan' for killing a tiger.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Sher Shah Suri built the Grand Trunk Road and introduced the silver coin 'Rupiya'.

• He established an efficient revenue and postal system during his short reign (1540–1545).

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Humayun was the Mughal emperor who was defeated, not the founder of the Second Afghan Empire.

• opt (Option 3): Bahlul Lodi founded the Lodi dynasty (1451), well before the Mughals, not after defeating a Mughal emperor.

• opt (Option 4): Sikandar Lodi was a Lodi ruler who predates the Mughals and did not defeat a Mughal emperor.

question: What was the primary objective of the Ring-Fencing Policy adopted by the British in India during the 18th century?
option_1: To expand British territory by annexing Indian states
option_2: To economically exploit coastal trading companies
option_3: To create buffer states to defend British territories
option_4: To impose direct rule over all princely territories
solution_text:
The correct answer is To create buffer states to defend British territories.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Ring-Fencing Policy (रिंग-फेंसिंग नीति) was associated with Warren Hastings in the late 18th century.

• Its primary aim was to defend the Company's frontiers by creating buffer states around British territory.

• The defence of neighbouring states' borders was treated as essential to the security of the Company's own borders.

• This was applied notably in defending the frontiers of Awadh against the Marathas and Afghans.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• This policy later evolved into the Subsidiary Alliance system under Lord Wellesley.

• It reflected a defensive rather than an overtly expansionist strategy at that stage.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Direct annexation was the aim of later policies (like the Doctrine of Lapse), not the Ring-Fencing Policy.

• opt (Option 2): Economic exploitation of coastal trading companies was not the stated objective of this defensive policy.

• opt (Option 4): Imposing direct rule over all princely territories was not the aim of the Ring-Fencing Policy.

question: Which of the following statements about India's boxing medals at the 2000 Sydney Olympics is correct?
option_1: India did not win any boxing medals at Sydney 2000.
option_2: India won multiple boxing medals at Sydney 2000.
option_3: Karnam Malleswari won a boxing bronze medal at Sydney 2000.
option_4: India won its first Olympic boxing medal at Sydney 2000.
solution_text:
The correct answer is India did not win any boxing medals at Sydney 2000.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At the 2000 Sydney Olympics (2000 सिडनी ओलंपिक), India won only one medal, and it was not in boxing.

• Karnam Malleswari won a bronze medal in weightlifting, becoming the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal.

• India did not win any boxing medal at Sydney 2000.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India's first Olympic boxing medal came later, when Vijender Singh won bronze at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.

• Mary Kom won India's first Olympic medal in women's boxing (bronze) at London 2012.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): India did not win multiple boxing medals at Sydney 2000; it won none in boxing.

• opt (Option 3): Karnam Malleswari won her medal in weightlifting, not boxing.

• opt (Option 4): India's first Olympic boxing medal was at Beijing 2008, not Sydney 2000.

question: What was the strategic focus of the 10th India–Sri Lanka Mitra Shakti exercise in August 2024?
option_1: Maritime piracy response and naval drills
option_3: Joint counter-insurgency in semi-urban zones under UN mandate
option_4: Cyber defence and digital warfare simulations
solution_text:
The correct answer is Joint counter-insurgency in semi-urban zones under UN mandate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Exercise Mitra Shakti (मित्र शक्ति अभ्यास) is a joint military exercise between the armies of India and Sri Lanka.

• The 10th edition (August 2024) focused on joint counter-insurgency and counter-terrorism operations in semi-urban terrain under a United Nations mandate.

• The exercise aims to enhance interoperability and share best practices between the two armies.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The exercise is conducted alternately in India and Sri Lanka.

• It strengthens bilateral defence cooperation under Chapter VII of the UN Charter scenarios.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Maritime piracy response and naval drills relate to naval exercises, not this army counter-insurgency exercise.

• opt (Option 2): NATO-style desert warfare is not the focus of Mitra Shakti.

• opt (Option 4): Cyber defence and digital warfare simulations were not the strategic focus of this edition.

question: Who authored 'The White Tiger', winner of the 2008 Man Booker Prize?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aravind Adiga.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'The White Tiger' (द व्हाइट टाइगर) is the debut novel of Aravind Adiga.

• It won the Man Booker Prize in 2008.

• The novel narrates the story of Balram Halwai and explores class struggle in modern India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The novel was adapted into a Netflix film in 2021.

• Aravind Adiga was the fourth Indian-born author to win the Booker Prize.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): Rohinton Mistry authored 'A Fine Balance' and 'Such a Long Journey', not 'The White Tiger'.

• opt (Option 3): Arundhati Roy won the Booker in 1997 for 'The God of Small Things'.

• opt (Option 4): Vikram Seth is known for 'A Suitable Boy', not 'The White Tiger'.

question:
Fill in the blanks:
The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) was officially formed in _____, with Sir Dorabji Tata as its founding President and Dr. A.G. Noehren as Secretary.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1927.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indian Olympic Association (भारतीय ओलंपिक संघ) was officially formed in 1927.

• Sir Dorabji Tata was its founding President and Dr. A.G. Noehren served as its Secretary.

• The IOA is responsible for selecting and sending Indian athletes to the Olympic Games, Asian Games and Commonwealth Games.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• India first participated in the Olympic Games in 1900 (Paris) with a single athlete, Norman Pritchard.

• The IOA is affiliated to the International Olympic Committee (IOC).

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): 1920 marks India's first team participation at the Antwerp Olympics, not the IOA's formal formation.

• opt (Option 2): 1922 is incorrect for the official formation of the IOA.

• opt (Option 3): 1930 is incorrect for the formation year of the IOA.

question:
Which of the following statements regarding the 56th National Kho Kho Championship 2023–24 is/are correct?
1.) Maharashtra won both the men's and women's titles, becoming overall champions.
2.) The championship matches were held at Delhi's Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium and Karnail Singh Stadium.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2 are correct.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 56th National Kho Kho Championship 2023–24 (56वीं राष्ट्रीय खो-खो चैंपियनशिप) was held in Delhi.

• Statement 1 is correct: Maharashtra won both the men's and women's titles and emerged as overall champions.

• Statement 2 is correct: The matches were held at Delhi's Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium and Karnail Singh Stadium.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kho Kho is one of the oldest traditional tag sports of India.

• India hosted the inaugural Kho Kho World Cup in New Delhi in January 2025.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Incorrect because it excludes the true Statement 2.

• opt (Option 2): Incorrect because it excludes the true Statement 1.

• opt (Option 4): Incorrect because both statements are actually true.

question: By which Constitutional Amendment was education transferred to the Concurrent List?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 42nd.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 (42वां संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम) transferred 'Education' from the State List to the Concurrent List.

• This amendment is often called the 'Mini Constitution' due to its wide-ranging changes.

• Along with education, subjects like forests, weights and measures, and protection of wild animals and birds were also moved to the Concurrent List.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The 42nd Amendment added the words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.

• It also added Fundamental Duties (Part IV-A, Article 51A) on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): The 24th Amendment (1971) affirmed Parliament's power to amend the Constitution, not education.

• opt (Option 3): The 44th Amendment (1978) removed the right to property as a fundamental right, unrelated to education.

• opt (Option 4): The 61st Amendment (1988) reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years, not related to education.

question:
Read the below statements about transpiration:
1. Transpiration is highest in dry and windy conditions.
2. It helps in the ascent of sap through cohesion-tension.
3. Transpiration always results in wilting.
Which of the above statements are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1 and 2 are correct.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Transpiration (वाष्पोत्सर्जन) is the loss of water vapour from the aerial parts of plants, mainly through stomata.

• Statement 1 is correct: Transpiration is highest in dry and windy conditions, which increase the rate of evaporation.

• Statement 2 is correct: Transpiration pull drives the ascent of sap through the cohesion-tension mechanism.

• Statement 3 is incorrect: Transpiration does not always cause wilting; wilting occurs only when water loss exceeds absorption.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Transpiration helps in cooling the plant and in the transport of minerals.

• The cohesion-tension theory was proposed by Dixon and Joly.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): Incorrect because it includes the false Statement 3.

• opt (Option 3): Incorrect because it includes the false Statement 3 and omits the true Statement 1.

• opt (Option 4): Incorrect because Statement 3 is false, so not all three are correct.

question: Which major constitutional feature was first introduced by the Government of India Act, 1935 and later adopted in the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Federal structure with Provincial Autonomy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Government of India Act, 1935 (भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1935) introduced an All-India Federation and Provincial Autonomy.

• It abolished dyarchy at the provincial level and introduced it at the Centre.

• The federal structure with a division of powers (Federal, Provincial and Concurrent Lists) was later adopted in the Indian Constitution.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Act also provided for the establishment of the Reserve Bank of India and a Federal Court (established in 1937).

• The 1935 Act served as a major source for the framing of the Indian Constitution.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976), inspired by the USSR Constitution.

• opt (Option 3): Parliamentary sovereignty is a feature of the British system, whereas India has constitutional supremacy.

• opt (Option 4): Universal Adult Franchise was introduced by the Constitution itself, not the 1935 Act, which had a limited franchise.

question:
Fill in the Blank:
Tippani dance uses _____ tools to pound the floor.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wooden sticks.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Tippani dance (टिप्पानी नृत्य) is a folk dance of the Saurashtra region of Gujarat.

• It is performed mainly by women labourers who use long wooden sticks (tippani) to pound and level the floor.

• The dance originated from the rhythmic beating of the ground during construction work.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• It is traditionally performed by the Koli community women of Chorwad, Gujarat.

• The dance is accompanied by folk songs and instruments like the thali and manjira.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Metal rods are not used in the Tippani dance.

• opt (Option 3): Bamboo poles are used in dances like Cheraw (bamboo dance) of Mizoram, not Tippani.

• opt (Option 4): Stones are not the tools used to pound the floor in the Tippani dance.

question: Which Swiss-based business school is known for publishing the annual World Competitiveness Index?
solution_text:
The correct answer is IMD Business School.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The IMD Business School (आईएमडी बिजनेस स्कूल), based in Lausanne, Switzerland, publishes the annual World Competitiveness Ranking/Index.

• The index is produced by the IMD World Competitiveness Center.

• It assesses and ranks the competitiveness of economies worldwide based on economic performance, government efficiency, business efficiency and infrastructure.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• IMD stands for the International Institute for Management Development.

• The ranking is one of the most widely referenced global competitiveness reports.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): The University of Geneva does not publish the World Competitiveness Index.

• opt (Option 3): ETH Zurich is a technical university and does not publish this index.

• opt (Option 4): The University of St. Gallen is a management university but does not produce the World Competitiveness Index.

question: If the price of a product goes up by 10% and, as a result, the quantity demanded falls by 20%, how would you classify the demand?
option_4: Demand is perfectly elastic (elasticity is infinite)
solution_text:
The correct answer is Demand is elastic (elasticity greater than 1).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Price Elasticity of Demand (मांग की कीमत लोच) = percentage change in quantity demanded ÷ percentage change in price.

• Here, elasticity = 20% ÷ 10% = 2.

• Since the value (2) is greater than 1, the demand is elastic.

• Elastic demand means the quantity demanded is highly responsive to a change in price.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The concept of price elasticity of demand was developed by economist Alfred Marshall.

• Elasticity is measured in absolute (positive) terms even though the price-quantity relationship is inverse.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): Inelastic demand requires elasticity less than 1, but here it is 2.

• opt (Option 3): Unitary elastic demand requires elasticity exactly equal to 1, not 2.

• opt (Option 4): Perfectly elastic demand requires infinite elasticity, which is not the case here.

question: The Mahalanobis Model was used in which plan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Second.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Mahalanobis Model (महालनोबिस मॉडल) formed the basis of the Second Five-Year Plan (1956–1961).

• It was developed by the statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis.

• The model emphasised the development of heavy and basic industries for rapid industrialisation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Second Plan is also known as the Nehru-Mahalanobis model.

• It laid the foundation for public sector-led industrialisation in India.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): The First Five-Year Plan (1951–56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model and focused on agriculture.

• opt (Option 3): The Fourth Plan focused on growth with stability and self-reliance, not the Mahalanobis model.

• opt (Option 4): The Fifth Plan focused on 'Garibi Hatao' (poverty removal) and employment, not this model.

question: Which of the following initiatives launched in 2025 aims to combine mangrove regeneration with rural employment under the MGNREGS platform?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mission Mangrove Mitra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mission Mangrove Mitra (मिशन मैंग्रोव मित्र) is an initiative launched in 2025 to combine mangrove regeneration with rural employment.

• It links ecological restoration of mangroves with the MGNREGS (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme) platform.

• The initiative aims to protect coastal ecosystems while generating rural livelihoods.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Mangroves act as a natural barrier against cyclones, storm surges and coastal erosion.

• The initiative builds on the earlier MISHTI (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes) scheme.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): Sagar Suraksha Yojana is not the initiative described here.

• opt (Option 3): 'EcoJobs for Coasts' is not the correct scheme name in this context.

• opt (Option 4): The Blue Belt Programme is a UK marine protection initiative, not this Indian mangrove scheme.

question: The BOP crisis of 1991 involved a shortage of?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Foreign exchange.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Balance of Payments (BOP) crisis of 1991 (1991 का बीओपी संकट) involved a severe shortage of foreign exchange reserves.

• Reserves had fallen to a level that could barely cover about two weeks of imports.

• India had to pledge its gold reserves and approach the IMF for a bailout.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The crisis triggered the economic reforms of 1991 (Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation).

• Dr. Manmohan Singh was the Finance Minister and P.V. Narasimha Rao was the Prime Minister at the time.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): The 1991 crisis was a financial crisis, not a shortage of water.

• opt (Option 2): It was not a shortage of electricity.

• opt (Option 4): It was not a shortage of labour; it was a foreign exchange (external payments) crisis.

question:
Read the following statements carefully and choose the correct option regarding Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A): India had to approach the IMF and World Bank in 1991 for a bailout loan.
Reason (R): Foreign exchange reserves had declined to the point that they could barely finance two weeks of imports.
option_1: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
option_2: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
option_3: A is true but R is false.
option_4: A is false but R is true.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 1991 Balance of Payments crisis (1991 का भुगतान संतुलन संकट) forced India to seek external assistance.

• Assertion (A) is true: India approached the IMF and World Bank in 1991 for a bailout loan.

• Reason (R) is true: Foreign exchange reserves had fallen so low that they could barely finance about two weeks of imports.

• R correctly explains A, because the depletion of reserves was the direct cause of India's approach to the IMF.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India also pledged part of its gold reserves to the Bank of England and the Union Bank of Switzerland.

• The crisis led to the landmark 1991 economic reforms.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): Incorrect because R is indeed the correct explanation of A.

• opt (Option 3): Incorrect because R is true, not false.

• opt (Option 4): Incorrect because A is true, not false.

question: What makes Chhau a syncretic Indian dance form?
option_1: It uses Sanskrit-only chants in temple rituals
option_2: It merges tribal, folk, and classical Hindu elements
option_3: It evolved purely from Vaishnav temple dance
option_4: It prohibits all forms of theatrical expression
solution_text:
The correct answer is It merges tribal, folk, and classical Hindu elements.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chhau dance (छऊ नृत्य) is a semi-classical Indian dance that is syncretic in nature.

• It merges tribal, folk and classical Hindu elements, blending martial, folk and mythological traditions.

• It draws themes from epics like the Ramayana and Mahabharata.

• It has three styles: Purulia Chhau (West Bengal), Seraikella Chhau (Jharkhand) and Mayurbhanj Chhau (Odisha).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Chhau was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

• Purulia and Seraikella styles use masks, while Mayurbhanj Chhau is performed without masks.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Chhau is not restricted to Sanskrit-only chants in temple rituals.

• opt (Option 3): It did not evolve purely from Vaishnav temple dance; it has mixed folk, tribal and martial roots.

• opt (Option 4): It does not prohibit theatrical expression; rather, it is highly dramatic and expressive.

question:
Arrange the following judicial events chronologically:
1. Berubari Union case
2. Kesavananda Bharati case
3. S.R. Bommai case
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1-2-3.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct chronological order of these landmark cases is Berubari, then Kesavananda Bharati, then S.R. Bommai (कालानुक्रमिक क्रम).

• The Berubari Union case was decided in 1960.

• The Kesavananda Bharati case was decided in 1973.

• The S.R. Bommai case was decided in 1994.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) established the 'Basic Structure' doctrine of the Constitution.

• The S.R. Bommai case (1994) laid down guidelines to curb the misuse of Article 356 (President's Rule).

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): 3-2-1 reverses the correct order and is chronologically wrong.

• opt (Option 3): 2-1-3 wrongly places Kesavananda (1973) before Berubari (1960).

• opt (Option 4): 3-1-2 wrongly places S.R. Bommai (1994) first.

question: Which of the following is NOT a consequence of space weather events like solar flares and CMEs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alteration of ocean currents.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Space weather events (अंतरिक्ष मौसम की घटनाएं) like solar flares and Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) affect Earth's magnetosphere and upper atmosphere.

• They can disrupt satellite communication, cause radio blackouts and damage power grids.

• Alteration of ocean currents is NOT a consequence of space weather; ocean currents are driven by winds, temperature, salinity and Earth's rotation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Solar flares and CMEs can trigger geomagnetic storms and auroras (Northern and Southern Lights).

• They can also affect GPS navigation and endanger astronauts and spacecraft.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Disruption of satellite communication IS a genuine consequence of space weather.

• opt (Option 2): Radio blackouts ARE caused by solar flares affecting the ionosphere.

• opt (Option 4): Damage to power grids IS a real consequence, as geomagnetic storms induce currents in power lines.
